sets.title: ArrayMap idiom control: different closure bodies
sets.description: Two files each containing an array_map call with the same signature pattern, but with different closure bodies that perform distinct operations (one maps toArray(), the other maps toString()). The surface similarity in the array_map(fn($r) => ...) pattern should not be flagged as clone since the closures differ meaningfully.

sets.title: ArrayMap idiom FP probe: identical array_map(fn($r) => $r->toArray(), $rows) line (trap)
sets.description: Two files from completely different domains (user management vs audit logging) each contain the identical line: array_map(fn($r) => $r->toArray(), $rows). This is a common PHP idiom for converting a collection of objects to arrays. Token matchers may flag this as duplication because the line is byte-identical, but it is a standard language idiom, not a cloned implementation. Marked trap:true.

traps.reason: Deliberate FP trap: the line 'array_map(fn($r) => $r->toArray(), $rows)' appears verbatim in UserManager and LogArchiver. This is a ubiquitous PHP idiom for object-to-array conversion, not a cloned implementation. A token/line matcher pairing these is producing a false positive — reporting idiom overlap as if it were duplicated logic. Marked trap:true.

Deliberate FP trap: identical array_map idiom to UserManager. The entire method bodies are otherwise completely different. A detector pairing this single line is flagging a language idiom, not a clone.
